cim: Alphabet Just Lost $500 Billion in Market Value. A Once-in-a-Generation Artificial Intelligence (AI) Opportunity Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight.
cim_eredeti: Alphabet Just Lost $500 Billion in Market Value. A Once-in-a-Generation Artificial Intelligence (AI) Opportunity Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight.
szoveg_eredeti:
Following Alphabet's (GOOGL -13.17%) (GOOG -12.94%) third-quarter earnings report on Oct. 28, shares plunged roughly 13% in early-morning trading on Thursday, wiping out $500 billion in market capitalization.

Indeed, investors have legitimate reasons to be concerned. Alphabet is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on artificial intelligence (AI), free cash flow has turned negative, and management is increasingly turning to the capital markets to help finance its infrastructure ambitions.

Nevertheless, I think Wall Street is overlooking something important: Alphabet is quietly assembling one of the most vertically integrated AI ecosystems in the world. The combination of custom AI chips, a rapidly expanding cloud business, and Google DeepMind research division is the foundation for a lucrative long-term investment opportunity.

Here's why I think the sell-off in Alphabet stock is an opportunity to buy the dip.

At first glance, Alphabet's third-quarter earnings looked impressive. Total revenue increased 25% year over year to $127.6 billion, while operating income rose 30% to $40.6 billion. However, analysts expected $128.2 billion in sales, meaning Alphabet fell short of Wall Street's forecast.

Google Search revenue increased 12% to $63.4 billion, a noticeable deceleration from the 17% growth in the second quarter. This slowdown reiterates the theory that popular chatbots such as ChatGPT or Claude are becoming formidable alternatives to Google, undermining the platform's appeal to advertisers.

Meanwhile, Alphabet reported earnings per share of $2.12, down from $2.87 a year earlier. It's important to note that part of this decline was due to an unrealized investment loss related to Space Exploration Technologies rather than actual profit erosion in Alphabet's core operations.

Perhaps the biggest concern involves cash flow. Alphabet generated $42.3 billion in operating cash flow during the third quarter. However, capital expenditures (capex) totaled $51.4 billion, resulting in a $9.1 billion free cash flow deficit.

Management doubled down on its 2026 capex budget, raising it to $195 billion to $205 billion and stressing that spending is expected to increase significantly next year. To support its infrastructure roadmap, Alphabet raised approximately $12.4 billion through common stock issuance and another $28.7 billion through debt issuance during the third quarter.

Issuing additional shares can dilute existing investors while borrowing increases future interest payments. These concerns help explain why investors are selling Alphabet stock. However, I see another side to this story.

I understand why Alphabet's spending is being scrutinized, but I think investors should pay closer attention to what that spending is building. During the third quarter, Google Cloud revenue surged 103% year over year to $30.7 billion. Even more impressive, the segment generated $11.1 billion in operating income, more than triple the amount reported a year earlier. Google Cloud's operating margin has expanded from 23.7% to 36.2% in just one year!

One of the underappreciated opportunities within the cloud computing landscape involves Alphabet's proprietary chips, known as Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). Unlike Nvidia GPUs, which serve a wide variety of applications, Google's TPUs are specialized processors designed to accelerate AI training and inference for specific workloads.

During its earnings call, management highlighted interest in the TPU architecture from Anthropic, Apple, Meta Platforms, and Oracle, as well as from financial institutions such as Citadel Securities and Jump Trading. This is important because it shows how Alphabet is selling complete AI computing systems and monetizing its investments in custom silicon beyond its own data centers.

Considering Google Cloud's backlog closed the quarter at around $561 billion, I think it's safe to say demand for the company's AI compute systems is high -- and accelerating.

Google DeepMind develops the frontier models that power Alphabet's AI products, including Gemini. The Gemini application now reaches 1 billion users, while Alphabet's AI model APIs process 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times the volume handled a year earlier.

These developments create opportunities that extend beyond chatbots. For example, Gemini is integrated into Google Search, Workspace, and Android, potentially improving engagement while creating new subscription and advertising opportunities. DeepMind's research also supports next-generation applications in agentic AI, autonomous systems, and quantum computing.

Alphabet's ownership of both AI models and underlying computing infrastructure creates a powerful economic advantage. DeepMind develops the models, TPUs provide the computing power, and Google Cloud distributes the technology to businesses and consumers. Few companies have this combination of proprietary hardware, software, cloud infrastructure, and global distribution.

To me, the market is becoming overly focused on Alphabet's near-term financial sacrifices while overlooking its long-term competitive positioning. With Google Cloud growing more than 100%, TPU adoption accelerating, and DeepMind continuing to develop new AI products, Alphabet's long-term upside is hard to dismiss.

For investors willing to tolerate volatility and hold shares for the long run, I think now is an attractive entry point to buy Alphabet stock.
